intents.name: Cache Locality & Memory Efficiency
intents.description: Optimize for data reuse and L1/L2 cache utilization through loop-level tiling and ordering transformations, reducing memory bandwidth pressure.
intents.rationale: On Broadwell, L1/L2 caches are small (32KB/256KB per core). Tiling loop nests to fit working sets into cache dramatically improves performance. This is the single highest-impact optimization for compute-bound kernels.

transformations.name: Tiling
transformations.description: Partition loop nest into cache-friendly tiles by introducing inner and outer loop levels, enabling reuse and reducing working-set size.
transformations.rationale: Tiling is fundamental for CPU performance on structured kernels (matmul, convolution, generic loops). Reduces memory bandwidth by a factor of tiling ratio; enables vectorization and parallelism of inner loops.
transformations.action_template: Tiling(tile_sizes) OR Tiling(loop_band, factors) OR Tiling(loop_id, factor)

transformations.name: Loop Interchange
transformations.description: Reorder loop dimensions to improve memory access patterns, regularize strides, and enable better vectorization or cache locality.
transformations.rationale: Loop interchange can convert irregular or long-stride access into unit-stride, improving cache behavior and vectorization potential. Often a secondary optimization after tiling.

transformations.name: Loop Peeling
transformations.description: Separate loop boundary conditions and edge cases from the main loop body, enabling optimization of the main loop without conditional overhead.
transformations.rationale: Allows inner loops to proceed without guard conditions, enabling vectorization and other aggressive optimizations. Reduces branch misprediction and conditional complexity.

intents.name: SIMD Parallelism & Vectorization
intents.description: Expose and exploit vector parallelism (AVX2, 256-bit SIMD) by restructuring loops for regular, aligned memory access and vectorizable operations.
intents.rationale: AVX2 on Broadwell provides 8 FP32 or 4 FP64 lanes. Vectorization can improve throughput by 4–8×. Essential for dense, regular kernels (matmul, convolution, elementwise). Requires aligned, strided access patterns.

transformations.name: Vectorization
transformations.description: Convert scalar loop nests into vector operations by exposing innermost loop parallelism as SIMD lanes, with proper alignment and stride assumptions.
transformations.rationale: Directly maps inner loop iterations to SIMD lanes, improving throughput. Most effective when memory access is unit-stride or regular. Prerequisite for achieving peak CPU performance on AVX2.

transformations.name: Loop Unrolling
transformations.description: Expand loop body by replicating iterations, increasing instruction-level parallelism and reducing loop overhead, enabling latency hiding and better register allocation.
transformations.rationale: Unrolling exposes ILP and amortizes loop control overhead. On CPUs with moderate issue width, moderate unroll factors (2–4) improve performance. Precedes vectorization in many pipelines.

transformations.name: Loop Jamming
transformations.description: Fuse adjacent or nearby loop nests into a single loop body, improving cache reuse and enabling better vectorization of merged iterations.
transformations.rationale: Reduces memory bandwidth by improving temporal locality between fused operations. Simplifies control flow for vectorization. Effective for fusible producer-consumer pairs or adjacent operations.

intents.name: Thread-Level Parallelism & Data Organization
intents.description: Distribute computation across multiple cores and optimize tensor layouts to support efficient coarse-grain parallelism and memory access patterns.
intents.rationale: On 28-core Broadwell, coarse-grain parallelism over outer loops is essential for scaling. Data packing (e.g., im2col) regularizes memory access and can reduce cache pressure and stride overhead.

transformations.name: Parallelization
transformations.description: Distribute outermost or appropriately chosen loop dimensions across worker threads using task-based or OpenMP-style parallelism, enabling multi-core scaling.
transformations.rationale: Maps logical loop parallelism to physical cores. Critical for scaling on 28-core systems. Typically applied to outermost parallel loops after inner loops are optimized via tiling and vectorization.

transformations.name: Packing / Data Layout Transformation
transformations.description: Reorganize tensor layouts (e.g., im2col for convolution, or tensor transposition) to regularize memory access patterns and reduce stride overhead.
transformations.rationale: Converts irregular access into regular, cache-friendly patterns. Example: im2col lifts convolution into a dense matmul-like operation. Amortized cost is often worthwhile for repeated kernels.
